scope: Corollary 6.4 (Budget for summably weighted templates) of the manuscript “Squared-logarithmic randomized k-server on arbitrary metrics” (preprints/Squared-logarithmic-randomized-k-server-on-arbitrary-metrics-September-24-2026/Squared-logarithmic-randomized-k-server-on-arbitrary-metrics-September-24-2026.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 110 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 db9f0de04f757cf3), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 38. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let templates be indexed by a finite or countable set I, with fixed weights ωα ≥ 0. Each template has fixed admissible parameters and the drift constant Cdr,α of Lemma 6.3. Assume A := ∑ α∈I ωα < ∞, B := ∑ α∈I ωαCdr,α < ∞. At each step, filter and drift the counting measure while keeping the previous functions gα,j fixed. Then edit these functions using the new history, retaining their template bounds. Suppose the weighted total potential drop in the edit stage is at least a nonnegative charge ct, taking ct = 0 on steps without edits. Then E ∑ t ct ≤ BℓQ + 2kA J ∑ j=1 rj ≤ BℓQ + 2kr0A τ − 1 . (6.25) In particular, if A, B are absolute constants, the multiplicative budget is O(ℓQ) and the additive bound is independent of the input law and horizon.
